facts.text: On this date in 1963, two giants died within hours of each other — Aldous Huxley and C.S. Lewis — but JFK's assassination that same day erased both deaths from the front pages.
On this date in 1869, the Suez Canal opened, instantly cutting the Europe-to-India sea route by over 7,000 kilometers and redrawing the entire map of global trade.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire continent of Australia — roughly 170 million versus 26 million.
Canada has more lakes than every other country on Earth combined, holding about 60% of the world's fresh lake water within its borders.
The city of Istanbul straddles two continents, but its European side holds only about 3% of Turkey's land while containing nearly 15 million of its residents.
On this date in 1963, trading on the New York Stock Exchange halted for the first time since WWII — not for a crash, but to mourn JFK's assassination. Markets reopened Monday, down 2.9%.
On this date in 2004, the Dow briefly crossed 10,000 for the third distinct time in its history, having fallen below that line twice after first breaching it in 1999.
The S&P 500 has historically risen more in the final two months of the year than in all other ten months combined — a pattern so reliable traders named it the Santa Claus Rally.
Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway owns enough of Coca-Cola that its annual dividend check from that single stock now exceeds what Berkshire originally paid for the entire position.
The Dutch East India Company, often called history's first publicly traded firm, had a peak valuation equivalent to roughly $8 trillion today — larger than Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia combined.

On this date in 1963, neurons across millions of brains encoded the same flash of horror simultaneously — the Kennedy assassination became one of the first globally shared traumatic memories, reshaping how scientists study collective recall.
Your skeleton is not static. Bone is constantly dissolving and rebuilding itself, replacing roughly 10% of its mass every year — the skeleton you have now is largely not the one you had a decade ago.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A teaspoon of its material would weigh about a billion tons on Earth.

On this date in 1977, Concorde began regular transatlantic service. At cruising altitude, passengers aged microscopically slower than those on the ground — time dilation at 60,000 feet is real and measurable.
The human eye can detect a single photon in complete darkness. Your visual system is operating at the absolute physical limit of light sensitivity.
On this day in 1963, JFK was assassinated — the same afternoon C.S. Lewis died. The world barely noticed Lewis; Dallas consumed everything.
Oxford University was teaching students before the Aztec Empire existed. It predates Tenochtitlán by roughly 200 years.
On this day in 1718, Blackbeard was killed off North Carolina. He had been a pirate for only about two years — his entire legend built in 24 months.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. She was separated from Khufu by 2,500 years.
The fax machine was invented before the telephone. Alexander Bain patented a working fax system in 1843; Bell's telephone came in 1876.
Sonder (n.): the realization that each passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in The Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, 2012. Already feels ancient.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a homesickness for a home you cannot return to — or one that never existed. No English word comes close, which is itself a kind of hiraeth.
On this day in 1963, Aldous Huxley died — overshadowed by Kennedy's assassination the same afternoon. He'd asked his wife to inject him with LSD as he lay dying. She did.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of used bookshops. Another Koenig coinage — the fact that it needed inventing says something about what bookshops actually are.
On this day in 1718, Blackbeard was killed off North Carolina. His logbook's final entry reads: 'such a day — rum all out.' The last word a pirate wrote was a noun of lack.
On Nov 22, 2010, Satoshi Nakamoto made his last substantive forum post before vanishing — signing off a reply about denial-of-service mitigations, with no farewell.
On Nov 22, 2021, Bitcoin's hash rate hit an all-time high just weeks after China's mining ban — exiled miners had quietly rebuilt capacity in the U.S., Kazakhstan, and Russia.
The Ethereum genesis block contains a hidden message: the hash of a 2015 Guardian article about a Greek bailout vote, mirroring Bitcoin's own embedded newspaper headline.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, sat in the codebase as a disabled no-op for years before BIP 65 activated it in 2015 — it was always there, just switched off.
Vitalik Buterin funded early Ethereum development partly by writing for Bitcoin Magazine at $1.50 per article — the whitepaper author was a teenage freelancer before he was a founder.
On this date in 2022, ChatGPT launched publicly. It reached 1 million users in 5 days — faster than any consumer product in history, including Instagram (2.5 months) and Netflix (3.5 years).

On this date in 2017, DeepMind's AlphaZero taught itself chess from scratch in 4 hours, then demolished Stockfish 8, the world's best conventional engine, winning 28 games and losing none in a 100-game match.
GPT-4 was trained on roughly 25,000 A100 GPUs running for 90–100 days. The electricity cost alone is estimated at $50–100M — before accounting for hardware, cooling, or staff.

Transformers, the architecture underlying nearly every frontier AI model, were introduced in a 2017 Google paper titled 'Attention Is All You Need.' Three of its eight authors left Google within two years to found competing AI labs.

The first neural network to defeat a human at Go, AlphaGo, did so in March 2016 — but it was already obsolete within 18 months. AlphaZero, trained purely through self-play, surpassed it without ever seeing a human game.
